newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields close down on improved prospects.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields close down on improved prospects.

text.p: Yields on both three-year corporate bonds and three-month CDs ended lower on Wednesday as strong buying emerged following the government's decision to supply more funds into the money market, traders said.
The Ministry of Finance and Economy said it planned to provide 2.0-2.5 trillion won in early February to ease tight liquidity caused by the Hanbo Group's financial crisis.
* Overnight average call rates unchanged at 12.5
Brokerage houses and investment trust companies were active shoppers despite large new issues, estimated at 140.4 billion won, brokers said.
The corporate bond yields are likely to stay below 12 percent for the time being, they said.
Three-month CD yields also fell on better short-term liquidity and increasing buying. Overnight call rates stood unchanged at an average of 12.5 percent.
